text: RBAC, least privilege, and segregation of duties are preventive — they try to stop a bad grant before it happens. Access reviews are detective: the recurring check that catches whatever slipped through anyway.

The defining feature isn't that someone runs a report — it's who signs off on it. IT can list everyone with access in minutes. What takes a real process is getting the data owner to attest, person by person: still needed, or remove it. Only the business owner actually knows which.

Most organizations review quarterly for sensitive systems, annually for lower-risk ones. But certain events trigger an unscheduled review too: a role change, a new audit finding, a security incident, a reorg or system integration.

Finding a problem is half the process. Remediation is actually fixing it — removing the flagged access, with an owner, a deadline, and confirmation it happened. Ten flagged grants that never get closed isn't a control, it's a to-do list.
Next up: privileged access — the smallest, most powerful set of accounts, and why they get a review process stricter than everything else in this chapter.
